key_insight: The paper shows that grid-state qubits can reach transmon-like state-preparation and measurement fidelity by combining repeat-until-success preparation with a more robust measurement protocol.
engineering_relevance: This reduces a major practical bottleneck for superconducting bosonic quantum error correction, making grid-state qubits more viable for scalable fault-tolerant hardware.
method: Repeat-until-success preparation of cardinal and magic states on a single-mode grid-state qubit
Improved measurement that compensates for finite-energy envelope effects and auxiliary-qubit readout errors
Measurement design tuned to increase robustness against photon loss
evidence_signal: Using both techniques together, the experiments report combined SPAM error below 10^-3, about two orders of magnitude better than prior state of the art.
watch_item: The result depends on high-performance QEC and specialized superconducting control, so scaling may still be constrained by hardware complexity and loss-induced errors.
paper_title: Quantum error correction of a grid-state qubit with state preparation and measurement errors below $10^{-3}$
